solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Portrays tourist as caustic, perhaps

parts.note: to portray someone is to paint them
a tripper is a day tourist or holidaymaker

explanation.surface: Someone depicts a sightseer as acid-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caustic' looks like a description of the tourist, but it is the definition, with 'perhaps' marking it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint stripper is often a caustic chemical, so a caustic substance is an example of one.

clue.text: In favour of case that's challenging

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the vocative is a grammatical case, used to address someone

explanation.surface: A supporter's argument turns out to be a tough one to take on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provocative challenges or goads people, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Children's author briefly raised dramatist

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
briefly asks for the author's name cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A writer for children, in short, was promoted to playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims NESBIT to NESBI, and 'raised' turns that upside down in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Schooled trio at art courses offered here

indicators.note: schooled means trained or put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three people trained at an art school took courses there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' looks like classes in an art school, but these are courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an Italian restaurant, a place where meal courses are served.

clue.text: Pain in most of mouth and windpipe

indicators.note: in places the pain word inside the shortened mouth word
most of asks for the mouth word less its final letter

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A sore mouth and throat, the symptoms of a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth' reads as anatomy alongside 'windpipe', but here it is the slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the anatomical name for the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Keen on grabbing right start

indicators.note: grabbing means the phrase for keen takes hold of the right letter inside it

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone eager seizes the correct beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a song or talk.

clue.text: Amazing things — height seen during revolutionary flower power

indicators.note: seen during places the height letter within the reversed flower and power
revolutionary means turned round, so the flower and power letters are read backwards

parts.note: the anemone is a flower
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: The hippie slogan 'flower power' at its height was something to marvel at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ANEMONE + P into PENOMENA, and 'seen during' puts H after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is a remarkable thing or person, and the plural keeps the number of 'things'.

clue.text: Fabulous bird to rise quickly? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word for rising quickly is kept

parts.note: prices rocket when they rise quickly

explanation.surface: A mythical bird that shoots skyward, or does it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', a nod to the rising bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend, so fabulous in the sense of found in fables.

clue.text: Fatality in plant — bug not involved

indicators.note: not involved means these letters are left out of the plant name

parts.note: bugloss is a bristly plant of the borage family, as in viper's bugloss
the word bug is taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect plays no part in a death at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the flowering plant; 'bug' is used literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a death, as in casualty reports of the losses in battle.

clue.text: A tap losing pressure — reach with difficulty

indicators.note: losing means the pressure letter is dropped from the word tap

parts.note: to stretch is to reach out

explanation.surface: A tap with no water pressure, which you can barely get to.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a stretch means only just managing it, an idiom for strain.

clue.text: First-class score against spinner

indicators.note: against means beside, so the spinner word is set next to the score word

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
to score is to cut a notch, or a notch is a tally mark

explanation.surface: An excellent tally made against a cricket slow bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket, but it is the child's spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal idiom for excellent, of the very highest quality.

clue.text: Two ducks crossing harbour in European city

indicators.note: crossing means the two noughts span the harbour word, one each side

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought, so two of them are two Os
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A pair of ducks swim across the harbour of a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.

clue.text: Actor, in turn, reviewed spy thriller

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked over again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Each actor in turn gave his opinion on a spy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn Curtain is a 1966 Hitchcock Cold War thriller about a defecting scientist.

clue.text: Tree died following onset of blizzard — tree in which you'll find rot

indicators.note: following places the tree and death letters after the blizzard letter
onset of means the first letter of blizzard is used

parts.note: the alder is a tree
D is the abbreviation for died in records
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree died in a snowstorm, and another tree has decay inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' looks like decay in wood, but it means nonsense; 'in which you'll find' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is nonsense, and rot is a British informal word for nonsense too.

clue.text: Surprisingly order a nun to leave without paying

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something unexpected, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a nun is commanded to slip off without settling the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: DO A RUNNER is British slang for leaving a restaurant or taxi without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang idiom means fleeing to dodge a bill, which matches leaving without paying.

clue.text: Stew at last in bistro? A controversial matter

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew, as in Lancashire hotpot

indicators.note: last in means the final letter of the word bistro is taken

explanation.surface: Is stew finally on the menu at a bistro? That is a contentious issue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lancashire hotpot is a British lamb and potato stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a delicate issue that people would rather not handle.

clue.text: Nobleman ahead of schedule? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word for ahead of schedule is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: early means ahead of schedule

explanation.surface: A lord arriving before time, or nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, a rank of the nobility.

clue.text: Victor getting in by way of examination

indicators.note: getting in means the Victor letter goes inside the phrase for by way of

parts.note: via means by way of
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A winner gains entry by means of a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral exam, notably the spoken defence of a doctoral thesis.

clue.text: Initiation of a hand during social event

indicators.note: during means the hand word sits inside the social event

parts.note: a dance is a social event
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone's first experience of a card hand at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is entry or admission, and initiation is a person's admission into a group.

clue.text: Lincoln has one, note

definitions.meaning: the seven-letter name Lincoln has the letter C in its exact middle
the musical note at the centre of the piano keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' suggests the president or the English city, but only its spelling matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the C nearest the centre of the piano, the reference musical pitch.

clue.text: Learn about vicious dog in stable

indicators.note: about means the learning word goes round the dog word

parts.note: to see is to learn or find out
a cur is a nasty or aggressive dog

explanation.surface: Discover there is a savage dog living in the horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a building for animals, but it is the adjective for firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure and stable are synonyms meaning firmly fixed and unlikely to give way.

clue.text: Distinctive character in quiet hostelry

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words quiet hostelry

explanation.surface: A peaceful inn with a character all its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a group or place.

clue.text: Did turn briefly in subtle comedy

indicators.note: in places the shortened turning word inside the word for subtle

parts.note: dry humour is subtle and understated

indicators.note: briefly means the past-tense word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: rolled means did turn, turned over

explanation.surface: A performer gave a short act in a low-key comic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did turn' reads like a music-hall act being performed, but it is a past-tense verb for turning over; 'subtle' gives the word used of understated humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is whimsical humour, a form of comedy or jesting.

clue.text: Coffee with dish, unlimited

indicators.note: unlimited means the dish word loses its outer limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: A coffee served alongside an endless supply of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with steamed milk.

clue.text: Relax wearing mate's fur

indicators.note: wearing means the relaxing word is worn inside the mate word, which wraps round it

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate = mate); the 's links
to chill is to relax

explanation.surface: Kicking back in a friend's fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a mate is a 'china', from 'china plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of the South American rodent, prized for coats.

clue.text: Buffet voucher doesn't include starter

indicators.note: doesn't include starter means the voucher word loses its first letter

parts.note: a chit is a note or voucher

explanation.surface: A meal ticket for a self-service spread that excludes the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' and 'starter' suggest a meal, but buffet is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike or batter repeatedly, so a hit is a blow of that kind.

clue.text: Most of group returned in carriage

indicators.note: returned means the shortened group word is read backwards
most of means the group word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: a party is a group

explanation.surface: Most of a party came back in a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a pony.

clue.text: Actors in rep he reviewed like dancing

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the words are looked at again in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic covered the actors in a repertory show.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Greek Muse of dance, so terpsichorean means relating to dancing.
